IR.rationale: A steepening curve signals improving growth and inflation expectations, which raise expected demand for commodities and their reflation premium.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield returns with stable spreads mark easy credit and risk-on conditions. These support financing of inventories and speculative and index flows into commodities.

V.rationale: Elevated commodity implied volatility tends to follow sell-offs and carries a risk premium paid to liquidity providers. That points to higher subsequent expected returns.

AP.rationale: Emerging-market equities capture news about EM growth, the marginal driver of commodity demand. Their strength leads and accompanies commodity gains.

ST.rationale: Equity momentum performing well indicates orderly trending markets without risk-off reversals. This is a weak positive backdrop for risky-asset returns.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar raises dollar commodity prices through the pricing channel, and a strong commodity currency confirms global demand. Together they define a commodity-friendly FX state.

COM.rationale: Commodity futures show documented time-series momentum, so recent broad basket gains tend to persist over weeks to months.

MC.rationale: Rising breakevens under loose financial conditions describe a reflationary regime, in which commodities as real assets tend to outperform.

ENDG.rationale: Own-index momentum in commodity futures is a well-documented return predictor at one- to thirteen-week horizons.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to policy rates signal flight to quality and downgraded growth outlooks. Both precede turbulent risk-asset markets.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with weak high-yield returns indicate tightening credit and deleveraging, which amplify commodity price swings.

V.rationale: Commodity implied volatilities embed forward-looking information on future realised variance beyond its own history.

AP.rationale: Equity declines raise leverage and risk aversion, which spill over into higher volatility across risky assets including commodities.

ST.rationale: Momentum losses typically occur in sharp market reversals and stressed regimes associated with elevated subsequent volatility.

FX.rationale: Yen strength combined with Aussie weakness is the classic carry-unwind, risk-off FX state. It accompanies volatile global asset markets.

COM.rationale: Commodity sell-offs strain inventories, margins and leveraged positions, so volatility tends to rise after negative basket returns.

MC.rationale: High financial stress reflects funding and liquidity strains that raise volatility across asset classes.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clustering means high recent realised variance carries information on its persistence beyond the baseline.

IR.rationale: Declining yields relative to policy rates signal weakening growth expectations and flight to safety, which precede commodity demand shocks.

B.rationale: Credit tightening forces deleveraging and inventory liquidation, raising the odds of a sharp commodity drawdown.

V.rationale: Jointly high commodity and equity implied volatility fattens the left tail of the forward return distribution.

AP.rationale: Weak emerging-market equities signal deteriorating EM demand and capital outflows, both key downside risks for commodities.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry little direct information about commodity left-tail events.

FX.rationale: A surging dollar tightens global dollar financing and mechanically depresses dollar commodity prices, raising crash risk.

COM.rationale: Negative commodity momentum and forced selling make further large losses more likely.

MC.rationale: Financial stress combined with falling inflation expectations describes a deflationary risk-off state, the typical setting of commodity crashes.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent own returns point to negative trend and elevated downside risk under commodity time-series momentum.

IR.rationale: Curve steepening reflects reflationary growth news that can trigger strong commodity rallies.

B.rationale: Strong US high-yield and EM sovereign returns signal broad risk appetite and EM financing relief, which favour sharp commodity upswings.

V.rationale: High commodity implied volatility widens the whole distribution and raises the chance of large rebounds after sell-offs.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equities indicate accelerating demand from commodity-intensive economies.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry little direct information about commodity right-tail events.

FX.rationale: A weak dollar together with strong commodity currencies is the FX configuration under which large commodity gains occur.

COM.rationale: Positive commodity momentum raises the chance of continued strong gains.

MC.rationale: Rising inflation expectations reflect reflationary news and inflation-hedging demand that can drive large commodity rallies.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent own returns signal a positive trend that raises the probability of large subsequent gains.
